# Lottie Theme

> A browser tool that recolours a Lottie animation between dark and light themes without
> After Effects. It finds every colour the file contains — including the ones no palette
> lists — proposes the opposite theme, and writes the result back. Files are processed in
> the browser: nothing is uploaded and there is no account.

The same logic ships three ways: a web editor, a `lottie-theme` CLI, and an MCP server so
an AI agent edits through the identical core. Nothing about how a colour is found or
changed is implemented twice.

Colour hides in eight different shapes of Lottie JSON — solid fills and strokes, animated
keyframes, gradient ramps and their separate alpha ramps, solid layers (`ty:1` → `sc`, a
hex string outside the shape tree), text, effect colours (a Drop Shadow's own colour,
which no palette built from fills will show), and PNGs embedded as data URIs. Naive
lightness inversion fails because of the last two: the effect colour is missed and the
bitmap stays dark, so a converted file shows dark halos and grey patches on a white page.

## Pages

- [Editor](https://lottie.italik.dev/editor): open a Lottie file, see every colour in it, and recolour it — solid fills, gradients, effects and embedded bitmaps
- [How Lottie stores colour](https://lottie.italik.dev/docs): the eight shapes a colour takes inside a Lottie document, and why each is easy to get wrong

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/ITalik-gr/lottie-theme): the monorepo — core, CLI, MCP server, live bridge and the web app
- [README](https://github.com/ITalik-gr/lottie-theme#readme): installing it, the CLI commands, and the MCP tool list
